The juvenile growth phase of the pod razor, Ensis siliqua, is characterized by the attainment of a critical developmental milestone during the larval-juvenile transition. Field surveys of recently settled spat indicate that metamorphosis is initiated once the prodissoconch reaches a shell length of 0.045 cm , a value consistent with the small size at which bivalve larvae typically become competent to undergo substratum attachment. Following this transformation, the post-metamorphic juveniles begin a rapid period of somatic expansion. The ultimate total length that individuals can achieve over their lifetime has been measured at 21.5 cm [Li = 21.5 cm], representing a substantial increase from the metamorphic benchmark. This considerable growth potential places Ensis siliqua among the larger members of the Solenidae family and reflects the species' adaptation to the dynamic intertidal and shallow subtidal sandflats it inhabits.

Reproductive maturation in Ensis siliqua is a gradual process tied closely to body size rather than strictly to chronological age. Histological examinations of gonadal tissue have established that functional puberty, defined by the onset of active gametogenesis, is reached when individuals attain a shell length of 11.2 cm [Lp = 11.2 cm]. This size threshold appears to be a reliable indicator of the switch in resource allocation towards reproductive effort. The gonadosomatic index (GSI) during the peak spawning period was recorded as 13% [GSI = 13%] at a stable water temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. It is worth noting that this index is based on mean whole-body wet weights of approximately 85 grams during the March to May period and drops to around 75 grams in the spent post-spawning condition of July and August, though these mass estimates carry some inherent uncertainty due to variable tissue hydration levels.

The early life history of the pod razor begins with the fertilised ovum, from which a tiny, yolk-dependent embryo develops. The wet weight at birth, representing the mass of the newly hatched trochophore or very early veliger larva, has been estimated at 0.0000000035 grams [Wwb = 0.0000000035 grams], a figure derived from the egg diameter of 0.0067 cm documented in the congeneric species Ensis directus. This minuscule initial mass underscores the extreme fecundity required for population maintenance. The age at birth, or more precisely the embryonic development time until eclosion, is approximately 5 days [ab = approximately 5 days] when development proceeds at a thermal regime of 13 °C [T = 13 °C]. These early life stages are entirely lecithotrophic, relying on endogenous yolk reserves before the veliger larva commences planktotrophic feeding on phytoplankton in the water column.

The ultimate wet weight attained by a fully grown, reproductively active adult of Ensis siliqua has been recorded at 110 grams [Wwi = 110 grams], although some online resources, such as the Encyclopedia of Life, report a higher maximum of 239 grams, suggesting considerable intraspecific variation depending on local environmental conditions and food availability. This substantial adult mass supports the species' high fecundity and its role as a dominant filter feeder in its ecosystem. The lifespan of the pod razor is not indefinite, with the maximum longevity documented at 7300 days [am = 7300 days] under field conditions measured at a consistent 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. This extended lifespan, exceeding two decades, allows for multiple reproductive seasons and is characteristic of many bivalve species inhabiting relatively stable, cold-water environments where metabolic rates are suppressed.

Comparative life-history analysis reveals that the pod razor's extended lifespan of 7300 days [am = 7300 days] is a notable trait among pholadid bivalves at a temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. This long generation time is coupled with the energetic investment in reaching the appreciable adult body mass of 110 grams [Wwi = 110 grams] at 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. The sustained somatic growth necessary to achieve a shell length of 21.5 cm [Li = 21.5 cm] places significant demands on the filter-feeding apparatus over the animal's life. The gonadosomatic index of 13% [GSI = 13%] was recorded at 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. The consistent environmental temperature of 10 °C likely exerts a strong influence on both the metabolic scope for growth and the timing of gametogenic cycles, ultimately shaping the species' characteristic life-history strategy.
